topic_title: Top 15 Best Dog Breeds for Apartment Living
intro: In an apartment, barking causes more trouble than size. A small dog that barks at every hallway sound will strain things with neighbors faster than a calm medium dog. After noise, look at energy, since an under-exercised dog paces and chews in a small space, and at how well the breed handles being alone for part of the day. Check your building's pet rules on weight and breed before you choose, and plan for daily walks, because even small dogs need time outside.

picks.description: The Cavalier is the most neighbor-friendly dog on this list: it rarely barks, it is gentle with everyone, and it gets along with children, cats and other dogs it meets in hallways and elevators. At 13 to 18 pounds it fits small spaces, and 30 to 45 minutes of walks and play a day is enough. The silky coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week. Cavaliers are easy to train but want company, so they struggle if left alone for long workdays. The breed is prone to heart conditions, so choose a breeder who health-tests parents.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers home often who want a gentle, quiet companion
picks.quirky_fact: Cavaliers often greet visitors with a wagging tail rather than barking, which makes them popular in shared buildings.
picks.skip_if: You work long hours away or can't budget for vet care

picks.description: The French Bulldog is one of the most popular city dogs for good reason: it is compact at under 28 pounds, rarely barks, and needs only moderate exercise of around 30 to 45 minutes a day. Frenchies are affectionate, playful and good with children and other pets, and the short coat needs little grooming. The trade-offs come from the flat face: Frenchies snore, overheat easily and can have breathing, spine and skin problems, so vet costs are often higher. Keep walks short in hot weather and choose a health-focused breeder.
picks.best_for: City dwellers wanting a quiet, low-maintenance, playful dog
picks.quirky_fact: Frenchies generally can't swim, so balconies near pools and lake trips need supervision.
picks.skip_if: You live somewhere hot without AC or can't budget for vet bills

picks.description: The Italian Greyhound is quiet, sleek and clean, weighing 7 to 14 pounds with a short coat that barely sheds. Indoors it is a calm, cuddly lap dog that seeks out warm blankets, and it rarely barks. It does need daily walks and an occasional chance to sprint in a secure area. IGs are gentle and good with other pets. The trade-offs are fragile legs that can break in falls from furniture, sensitivity to cold, and house-training that can be slow, especially in bad weather.
picks.best_for: Quiet apartments wanting a clean, cuddly, low-shedding small dog
picks.quirky_fact: Italian Greyhounds often need a sweater on cold walks because of their thin coat and low body fat.
picks.skip_if: You have rough young children or live somewhere very cold

picks.description: The Japanese Chin is one of the calmest, quietest small breeds, weighing 7 to 11 pounds and rarely barking. Short walks and indoor play meet its exercise needs, which suits apartment life. Chins are gentle, affectionate and good with children, cats and other dogs, and they keep themselves clean like cats. The silky coat sheds moderately but rarely mats with weekly brushing. Their flat faces make them sensitive to heat, so they need air conditioning in summer.
picks.best_for: Calm apartment dwellers wanting a quiet, low-exercise lap dog
picks.quirky_fact: Japanese Chins like to perch on the back of sofas, much like cats.
picks.skip_if: You want a jogging partner or live somewhere hot without AC

picks.description: The Havanese is cheerful, sturdy and easy to train, weighing 7 to 13 pounds and getting along with children, cats and other dogs. Its moderate energy is met with a couple of walks and indoor play. The long, silky coat sheds little but needs brushing several times a week, or a short puppy clip with professional trims. Havanese bark to alert, but are not usually nuisance barkers. Their biggest need is company: they can develop separation anxiety if left alone for long periods.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers home often who want a happy, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Havanese often live 14 to 16 years, longer than many breeds.
picks.skip_if: The dog will be alone for long workdays

picks.description: The Boston Terrier is compact, friendly and easy to train, with a short coat that sheds lightly and needs almost no grooming. It weighs 12 to 25 pounds and needs around 30 to 45 minutes of exercise daily. Bostons get along with children and other pets and adapt well to apartments, though some bark at the door. Like other short-muzzled breeds, they snore and struggle in heat, so walks move to cooler hours in summer.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting an easy-care, playful small dog
picks.quirky_fact: Boston Terriers are often called the American Gentleman for their tuxedo markings.
picks.skip_if: You live somewhere hot without air conditioning

picks.description: The Maltese is a gentle toy dog under 7 pounds with low energy and an easy-to-train nature, which makes it simple to keep in a small space. It is affectionate and good with other pets. The long, white, silky coat sheds little but needs daily brushing or a short puppy clip with regular grooming, plus cleaning around the eyes. Maltese can bark at sounds, so early training on a quiet cue helps neighbors. They dislike being left alone for long.
picks.best_for: Calm adults in small apartments wanting a tiny, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Despite its long white coat, the Maltese has no undercoat, so it sheds very little.
picks.skip_if: You won't keep up with grooming or will often leave it alone

picks.description: The Shih Tzu is a calm, friendly small dog with low exercise needs, around 20 to 30 minutes a day, that is happy to spend much of its time indoors. It gets along with children and other pets. The long coat sheds little but tangles quickly, so brush daily or keep a short clip with regular grooming. Shih Tzus can be stubborn to house-train and may bark at the door. Their short muzzle makes them sensitive to heat.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a calm, low-energy lap dog
picks.quirky_fact: Shih Tzus were bred to be indoor companions, which suits apartment life.
picks.skip_if: You want a quick learner or live somewhere very hot

picks.description: The Bichon Frise is cheerful, easy to train and good with children and other pets, weighing 12 to 18 pounds. Its curly coat sheds very little but needs brushing most days and a professional trim every four to six weeks. Energy is moderate, met with walks and indoor play. Bichons may bark at the door, and house-training can take longer than average. They dislike long stretches alone, so they suit people who are home often.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a cheerful, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Bichons are known for sudden bursts of zoomies around the room.
picks.skip_if: You won't brush daily or pay for regular grooming

picks.description: The Miniature Schnauzer is small, sturdy and easy to train, weighing 11 to 20 pounds with a wiry coat that sheds little. It needs about 45 minutes of activity daily and gets along with children and other pets. The main apartment consideration is barking: Minis are alert watchdogs and will announce visitors, so teach a quiet cue early. The coat needs weekly brushing and clipping every six to eight weeks.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a sturdy, low-shedding watchdog
picks.quirky_fact: Miniature Schnauzers were bred as farm ratters in Germany.
picks.skip_if: Your building has thin walls and you can't train a quiet cue

picks.description: The Pug is a compact, affectionate clown of 14 to 18 pounds with moderate exercise needs, around 30 minutes a day. It is friendly with children and other pets and adapts easily to small spaces. The short coat sheds more than you'd expect and needs weekly brushing, and facial wrinkles need regular cleaning. Pugs snore and overheat easily because of their flat faces, and they are prone to weight gain and eye problems, so measured meals and vet care matter.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a playful, affectionate companion
picks.quirky_fact: A group of Pugs is called a grumble.
picks.skip_if: You dislike shedding and snoring or live somewhere hot

picks.description: The Brussels Griffon is a small, bearded toy dog of 8 to 10 pounds with a big, expressive face. It sheds little and needs modest exercise, so it fits small spaces easily. Griffons bond tightly with their person and are affectionate, but they can be stubborn and sensitive, and they bark at unusual sounds. The rough coat needs brushing and occasional hand-stripping; the smooth coat needs less. They do best with adults who are home often.
picks.best_for: Adults home often who want a small, characterful, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Brussels Griffons were originally kept to catch rats in Belgian stables.
picks.skip_if: You want a quiet dog for thin walls or will leave it alone often

picks.description: The Lagotto Romagnolo is a medium dog of 24 to 35 pounds, larger than the others here, but its moderate energy and affectionate nature make it workable in a roomier apartment. It sheds little thanks to its dense curls, which need regular brushing and clipping. Lagottos need about 45 to 60 minutes of activity daily, including nose work, and they get along with children and other pets. Some can be vocal or sensitive to noise, so training helps.
picks.best_for: Owners of larger apartments wanting a medium, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Lagottos are the only breed recognized specifically as truffle-hunting dogs.
picks.skip_if: You have a small studio or won't commit to regular grooming

picks.description: The West Highland White Terrier is a sturdy, cheerful little terrier of 15 to 20 pounds that adapts to apartments if it gets daily walks and play. It is friendly and good with children and other pets, though terrier instincts mean it may chase small animals. The rough white double coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week plus regular trimming. Westies bark to alert and can dig, so they need training and enough activity.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a sturdy, cheerful small terrier
picks.quirky_fact: Westies were bred white so hunters could tell them apart from foxes.
picks.skip_if: You need a very quiet dog or dislike regular grooming

picks.description: The Scottish Terrier is a compact, dignified terrier of 18 to 22 pounds that does fine in an apartment with daily walks. It is loyal to its family but independent and reserved with strangers. The wiry coat needs weekly brushing and regular trimming. Scotties bark to alert, and the dataset flags them as not good with cats or other dogs, which matters in buildings full of pets. They suit experienced owners in single-pet homes.
picks.best_for: Experienced owners in single-pet homes wanting a loyal terrier
picks.quirky_fact: Scottish Terriers have appeared on the Monopoly board as a playing piece.
picks.skip_if: You have other pets or want an outgoing, social dog

faqs.question: What is the best dog for a small apartment?
faqs.answer: Quiet, small breeds with moderate energy suit small apartments best. The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, French Bulldog, Italian Greyhound and Japanese Chin are strong choices because they rarely bark and are content indoors after daily walks.

faqs.question: Which apartment dogs bark the least?
faqs.answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, French Bulldog, Italian Greyhound and Japanese Chin are all rated low for barking. Training still matters: teach a quiet cue early, and avoid leaving any dog bored and alone for long stretches.

faqs.question: Can large dogs live in apartments?
faqs.answer: Some can. Calm large breeds such as Greyhounds and Mastiffs often adapt well if they get daily exercise, while high-energy large breeds struggle. Building weight limits are usually the bigger obstacle, so check your lease first.

faqs.question: How do I keep an apartment dog happy?
faqs.answer: Give at least one or two daily walks, add puzzle toys or short training games for mental exercise, keep a predictable routine, and consider a dog walker or daycare on long workdays. A tired, mentally stimulated dog is a quiet neighbor.

faqs.question: Which apartment dogs are good for people who work all day?
faqs.answer: No dog should be alone for very long days without a midday break. Calmer, more independent breeds such as the Italian Greyhound or French Bulldog cope better than people-focused breeds like the Havanese or Cavalier. A dog walker is a good solution for long hours.

seo_title: 15 Best Apartment Dogs for Small Spaces (2026)
answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, French Bulldog and Italian Greyhound are the best apartment dogs here: small, rarely barking and content with moderate exercise. For apartments, noise matters more than size, so prioritize low-barking breeds and plan on daily walks whatever you choose.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for small and medium breeds with low or medium energy and no high barking rating, then ordered them by barking level, size, trainability and how well each gets along with neighbors' pets, putting the quietest, most adaptable breeds first.
author: Elena Marsh
